summary: Step 81 (final file of batch B0023): asks whether KnowledgeOS can actually determine relevant system state from what it observes -- the boundary between having data and having sufficient information. Formalizes observation as a projection O_t=H(S_t), observational equivalence S_1~_H S_2 iff H(S_1)=H(S_2), and identifiability of a property Q (Q identifiable iff H(S_1)=H(S_2) implies Q(S_1)=Q(S_2); otherwise NotIdentifiable -- 'a major safeguard against false architectural certainty'), and observability (whether S_0 can be reconstructed from O_0:T and u_0:T-1). Gives the architectural principle 'no observation -> no justified claim' / absence-of-evidence≠evidence-of-absence (observed NoViolationFound cannot license ViolationDoesNotExist), a Coverage(Q,O) concept warned against being collapsed to an unjustified single percentage, measurement design (adding observations to improve identifiability, connected to Step 75's Value of Information), ObservationDesign=f(DecisionNeeds,Uncertainty,Cost,Risk) (more telemetry ≠ more observability -- an ObservabilityGap example with irrelevant signals), a taxonomy of architecture-relevant observation types (SourceDependencies, RuntimeDependencies, APIContracts, DeploymentTopology, Configuration, InfrastructureState, SecurityControls, ChangeHistory) each a different state projection, multiple disagreeing observation sources (O^repo, O^runtime, O^infra, O^governance, O^human) requiring StateConflict representation rather than silent overwrite, source-specific authority (Runtime authoritative for CurrentlyRunningVersion vs Git for CommittedVersion, CommittedState≠DeployedState) and a DDD ubiquitous-language collision (undifferentiated 'version' collapsing SourceVersion/BuildVersion/DeploymentVersion/RuntimeVersion is a FAIL), a formal Observation=(Source,Timestamp,Context,Method,Value,Confidence,Provenance) record, observation staleness/freshness with context-dependent FreshnessThreshold and temporal validity (ValidAt(t_o) vs ValidAt(t_now), StaleForCurrentState), state estimation under uncertainty that must not collapse a 51/49 split to certainty, decision-aware state estimation and DecisionRelevantObservability (uncertainty over a state dimension is irrelevant if it does not change the decision; becomes critical when it would), ObservationQuality vs ObservationQuantity and correlated-observation deflation (100 signals from one sensor, or five agents repeating one document, are not independent confirmations -- EvidenceCount=1), the ArchitecturePrinciple->FormalProperty->RequiredObservations->Verifier->GovernanceDecision formalization pipeline, the ComplianceUndetermined result when a required observation is unavailable (not defaulting to Compliant), three-valued (True/False/Unknown) and four-valued (Compliant/NonCompliant/Unknown/NotApplicable) governance logic with Unknown≠Failure and NotApplicable as a distinct DDD domain semantic (not null/false), ObservabilityDebt (gap between DesiredGovernance and AvailableEvidence) driving a GovernanceRule->ObservationRequirement->EngineeringCapability->Evidence->Governance self-improving loop, the Step 81 deeper result ('a governance claim is only as strong as the observability and identifiability of the property it asserts'), five new invariants (I_Identifiability, I_Unknown, I_ObservationProvenance, I_DecisionRelevantObservability, I_EvidenceIndependence), verdict STEP 81 PASS with the concluding True/False/Unknown reasoning pattern contrasted against conventional if-not-violation-then-compliant logic -- twenty-nine experiments (28 PASS, 1 FAIL). Closes with a short preview of Step 82 (uncertainty propagation through Observation->Measurement->Inference->CausalModel->Decision, avoiding 'High uncertainty -> False precision'), which is outside batch B0023 and not further extracted.
contribution_assessment: The batch's final file: a rich, self-contained formalization of observability/identifiability as the epistemic foundation underneath Step 80's control-feedback governance model. Introduces identifiability and observational equivalence, absence-of-evidence reasoning, coverage/measurement design, multi-source observation conflict and source-specific authority, a formal Observation record with provenance/staleness, decision-relevant (not full) observability, evidence-independence deflation for correlated signals, a three/four-valued governance logic (Unknown and NotApplicable as first-class, non-collapsible states), ObservabilityDebt, and five new invariants. Explicitly ties into Step 75 (Value of Information) and the multi-agent independence work. Ends with an out-of-batch preview of Step 82 (uncertainty propagation), recorded only as an open/future-research note, not extracted.
